name: FinanceDatabase 2.5.2
html:
2.5.2 continues the data-quality work of 2.5.1, with checks across the whole database that were each verified against a source, and better primary listings for companies abroad. The hosted MCP server now shows a setup page and a usage dashboard when it is opened in a browser. It also includes fixes from contributors, and from this version on, releases are published by GitHub Actions after an approval.

Package

  • Filtered selections keep to_toolkit(). Slicing or filtering the result of select() or search(), for example selection[selection["market_cap"] == "Large Cap"], now returns a FinanceFrame instead of a plain DataFrame (#255, thanks @wavebyrd).
  • An empty search list matches nothing instead of raising an error, e.g. fd.Equities().search(name=[]) (#252, thanks @jackiectl2).
  • Better primary listings for only_primary_listing. Countries without a main venue get a home venue, home lines on a country's own venue come first, and lines with an ISIN win at home. Avon now resolves to AVON.L, FACC to Vienna and STMicroelectronics to Paris (#243).

MCP server

  • A setup page in the browser. Opening https://financedatabase.jeroenbouma.com/mcp (or /) in a browser shows how to add the server in three steps, instead of a "Not Acceptable" error. MCP clients are unaffected (#245, #247).
  • A usage dashboard at /stats in the browser: key figures, calls and users per day, and the most used tools. Scripts still get the JSON (#248).
  • Missing numbers are null in tool answers instead of non-standard NaN tokens (#254, thanks @jackiectl2).
  • Infinite limits and offsets fall back to the default instead of failing (#249, thanks @jackiectl2).
  • Setup wizard (financedatabase-mcp-setup):
    • It writes Claude Desktop's config to ~/.config/Claude/ on Linux, which is where Claude Desktop reads it.
    • It adds Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf (~/.config/devin/, or %APPDATA%\devin\ on Windows).
    • Older Windsurf installs remain an option (#256).

Data

  • Correctness and quality checks across the whole database, each change verified against an exchange list, filing or other public source (#244):
    • delisted and re-tickered lines updated;
    • bonds, warrants and certificates removed from equities;
    • tokenized stocks removed from cryptocurrencies;
    • SPACs moved to Capital Markets;
    • new Korean (KRX) and Thai (SET) companies added;
    • US ETF delistings are now recorded by the weekly update.
  • Consistent listings (#242). A company's listings now share one country, industry and market cap tier. Blank identifiers and categories are filled from the share's other listings.
  • Corrected names and categories: SAP SE, Meta Platforms, Inc., Tencent Holdings Limited and Toyota Boshoku (#246).

Releases

  • Releases are built and published by GitHub Actions after an approval. This covers the package on PyPI, the GitHub release with financedatabase.mcpb and the MCP Registry entry (#257).

name: FinanceDatabase 2.5.1
html:
2.5.0 introduced the MCP server and a cleaned-up database. 2.5.1 is about keeping that database current without manual work, and about making the MCP server's answers trustworthy. Sampling hundreds of real searches on the hosted server showed where results went wrong: depositary receipts or foreign regional lines shown as a company's main listing, funds and bonds filed as equities, stale data, and accent or spelling variants that found nothing. Each fix below is a general, data-derived rule rather than a list of exceptions, so it keeps working as the data changes every week.

Funds and money markets are retired

Funds and money markets are no longer maintained. The decision followed a scan of how current they were:

  • Badly out of date. Compared with Nasdaq's list of US funds (tickers A to I):

    • 42% of the US mutual funds in the database are no longer listed: they were merged, liquidated or matured, often unit trusts with a fixed end date;
    • 47% of the funds listed today are missing.

    Money markets looked the same: 40% are no longer listed, and only 352 of the 970 money market funds listed in that range are present.

  • No source to keep them current. Mutual and money market funds aren't traded on an exchange, so there is no public, official directory that lists them worldwide, unlike stocks and ETFs. The roughly 27,000 non-US funds (Morningstar IDs; funds on Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Madrid, Vienna and Mexico) have no public source at all. Keeping them current would mean scraping fund portals or relying on paid data, which this project doesn't do.

  • No way to mark closures. Funds have no ISIN or delisted column, so a closed or merged fund can't even be flagged; it just stays in the data as if it still existed.

  • Little use. In the MCP server's usage statistics, funds were among the least called asset classes.

An outdated answer is worse than no answer, especially for an AI assistant that presents it confidently, so the classes were retired rather than left to decay further:

  • Python package: fd.Funds() and fd.MoneyMarkets() still load their data unchanged, but warn when loaded (FutureWarning) that it's no longer maintained. Existing code keeps working.
  • MCP server: the funds and moneymarkets tools are removed, and both classes are left out of search_instruments, show_options and search_categories, so an assistant never returns them.
  • Exchange-listed funds move to ETFs. Funds that trade on a main stock exchange under an ordinary ticker do have a public source and stay maintained: the Chinese LOFs, the listed funds on Euronext Amsterdam (Kempen, Actiam, ASN), Copenhagen, Milan, Jakarta and a few others. A fund qualifies when its symbol has the shape of that exchange's real tickers. Spanish SICAVs therefore stay retired: their symbols are CNMV registry numbers, and most left the exchange after Spain's 2022 tax change.

The database's own equity classification (breaking)

Equities are now classified in the database's own three levels, listed in scripts/categories.json.

  • Sectors: the 11 names are unchanged.
  • Industry groups and industries: they have new names, for example:
    • Media, Entertainment & Internet;
    • Semiconductors & Chip Equipment;
    • Payments & Specialty Finance;
    • Consumer Lending;
    • Rail & Road Transport.
  • New structure:
    • REITs are split by property type.
    • Real estate companies that aren't REITs have their own industry.
    • Savings banks stay Banks, and other mortgage lenders become Mortgage Finance.

This is a hard switch: filters on an old industry group or industry name return nothing. fd.show_options("equities") lists the new names.

MCP server

  • Results by relevance.
    • Exact symbol and name matches come first, followed by the same company's listing on its largest exchange (ASML.AS, then ASML on NASDAQ).
    • Asset classes take turns, so a search such as "bitcoin" shows the coin, ETFs, companies and indices together.
    • A query without spaces matches whole words: loreal finds L'Oréal, but toyota no longer finds Toyo Tanso.
  • Primary listings worked out from the data. only_primary_listing keeps a company's real home listing. It leaves out:
    • euro lines of US companies on German regional exchanges;
    • Canadian depositary receipts (CDRs) and similar local receipts;
    • mandatory convertible preferreds;
    • duplicate share classes (one of BRK-A and BRK-B).
  • Forgiving filters.
    • Filter values ignore accents (curacao → Curaçao).
    • A synonym list maps common alternatives to the database's values: Côte d'Ivoire → Ivory Coast, USA, UK, Holland, Korea, Czechia; sectors such as Tech or Healthcare; and tiers such as megacap.
  • search_instruments adds a delisted column when include_delisted is on.
  • Unique users in /stats. A user is a keyed hash (HMAC) of the address and user agent, and neither is ever stored raw. PRIVACY.md describes this.
  • Reliability.
    • Computing listing ranks for funds and indices no longer needs several gigabytes of memory; it used to restart a small server.
    • Ties are broken the same way every time, so results don't change between restarts.
    • Under a test load of 20 simultaneous users, the hosted server answers every call within seconds.
  • Server name: the server is named "Finance Database".
  • Primary listings across borders.
    • A venue counts by the listings of its own country, so Airbus is AIR.PA rather than a German regional line.
    • Brazilian depositary receipts (BDRs) are never a primary listing.
    • Abroad, the line with the share's ISIN wins (Glencore stays GLEN.L).
  • Clearer answers.
    • Asking for funds or money markets explains that they are retired and still available in the Python package.
    • A currency's name finds its pairs ('japanese yen').

Package

  • fd.Funds() and fd.MoneyMarkets() warn that they're no longer maintained (see above).
  • The primary-listing logic (listings_model.py) gains the rules described under the MCP server. ETFs and indices, which have no country, keep their primary listings.

Database

  • ETFs.

    • European ETFs from Xetra, Euronext and SIX were added, among them many 2025–2026 launches and new lines of popular funds such as VWCE.AS and SPYL.AS. These exchanges publish only abbreviated names, so full names come from the same fund's other listings or its Börse Frankfurt / Euronext page.
    • Tickers that were replaced are marked delisted (e.g. Xtrackers' old DBX* tickers on Xetra).
    • US ETFs that couldn't be added because an old company held their ticker were moved over (e.g. the Sprott physical trusts).
    • Blank categories are filled from the fund's other listings, or from name words that clearly decide a category ("treasury" → Fixed Income / Treasury Bonds). Issuer names decide nothing, and a category always comes with its group. The rule is right about 94% of the time on ETFs with known categories.

  • Cryptocurrencies. Coins in CoinGecko's top 500 were added (such as Sui, Shiba Inu, NEAR, Pepe), and coins that no longer exist were removed. Numbered duplicates of a coin (SOL1, DOT1, UNI3) were removed.

  • Currencies. The list now follows ISO 4217: new currencies (SLE, ZWG, VED, XCG) were added, and withdrawn ones (HRK and BGN after the euro, SLL, ANG, CUC) removed.

  • Indices.

    • The indices Euronext publishes were added, plus the missing headlines MSCI World and the SSE Composite.
    • ETF iNAVs take the categories of the index they track.

  • Equities.

    • Bonds, notes, warrants, certificates and other papers that aren't company shares were removed, and are kept out from now on.
    • Lines of securities whose home listing is delisted were marked delisted (e.g. the old Royal Dutch Shell A/B lines).
    • Chinese funds were moved out of equities.
    • ISINs were filled from CUSIPs and from symbols that are ISINs.
    • Names and countries were corrected (Aegon Ltd., Curaçao instead of the former Netherlands Antilles).

  • Classification and countries reviewed.

    • Every large and mega cap company's classification was checked against its business description, with 347 corrections (e.g. Philips → Medical Devices & Supplies, Visa and Mastercard → Payments & Specialty Finance).
    • Smaller companies without an industry, or whose listings disagreed, were classified the same way (3,233 newly classified, 706 conflicts resolved).
    • Wrong and blank countries were corrected where the company's description and its exchange or ISIN agree, e.g. Malaysian companies marked Japan.

  • Listing status.

    • US equities were checked against the Nasdaq Trader directory: 803 rows were delisted and 15 relisted.
    • Lines abroad of shares delisted at home are delisted too, e.g. Electronic Arts and Twitter in Germany.
    • Ferrovial SE's Euronext Amsterdam listing was added.

  • ETFs.

    • 16,786 mutual funds were removed from the German regional ETF files.
    • 4,430 regional ETF lines took the ISIN, full name and categories of their Xetra line.

  • Non-shares. More instruments that aren't company shares are recognised and removed: debentures, Nordic knock-out certificates, subscription warrants, rights issues and listed indices.

Weekly update

  • What it maintains. The weekly update now maintains every live asset class, not just US equities. New sources sit next to the existing exchange directories (Nasdaq Trader, HKEX, NSE, JPX, ASX, TSX):
    • Xetra, Euronext and SIX for ETFs;
    • CoinGecko for cryptocurrencies;
    • ISO 4217 for currencies;
    • Euronext for indices.
  • US listing status. The weekly update now compares the US equities with the Nasdaq Trader directory and keeps their delisted flag current, with a guard against implausibly many delistings.
  • Where the code lives. database_update.yml holds no Python anymore. scripts/ follows the package's MVC layout, and scripts/README.md documents every rule.
  • Robustness, so an automated run can't damage the database:
    • downloads are retried with backoff;
    • each source runs on its own, so a failure skips only that source;
    • files are only rewritten when they change, through a temporary file;
    • implausible changes are skipped (for example, a large share of market cap tiers changing at once);
    • scripts/check_database.py compares each update with the last commit and undoes it before the commit if it would introduce duplicate symbols, symbols in two asset classes, changed columns or a large loss of rows.

Documentation

  • The README's Questions & Answers describe what the weekly update maintains and from which public sources, and why funds and money markets were retired.
  • The README's MCP section follows the Finance Toolkit's format and links to the MCP page for the tools, examples and self-hosting.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.5.0
html:
The biggest update since the 2.0 release: a faster package built on Polars and a database that has been cleaned, verified and filled in almost everywhere. The API is unchanged, so existing code keeps working; only the minimum Python version moves to 3.11.

The Finance Database MCP Server

This release introduces an MCP server that gives any AI assistant supporting the Model Context Protocol direct access to all 300,000+ symbols. Ask in plain English for, say, every large cap semiconductor company in Europe, the fixed income ETFs of an issuer or the listings behind an ISIN, and the assistant queries the database for you. No API key is needed.

  • Hosted: connect to https://financedatabase.jeroenbouma.com/mcp; nothing to install and no sign-in.
  • Local: uvx --from "financedatabase[mcp]" financedatabase-mcp-setup adds the server to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI or Windsurf. The Claude Desktop bundle (financedatabase.mcpb) is attached to this release.
  • Tools: one per asset class (equities, etfs, funds, indices, currencies, cryptos, moneymarkets) with the same filters as select(), plus search_instruments (find a symbol by ticker, name or ISIN), show_options and search_categories. Responses are compact and paginated, and invalid filter values come back with suggestions.
  • Self-hosting: financedatabase-mcp --transport streamable-http or the included Docker setup, with /health and, when FD_MCP_ANALYTICS=1, anonymous usage totals at /stats.

See the MCP Server section of the README for every client.

Package

  • Faster, lazily evaluated queries with Polars. The database is downloaded once into a local cache (checked for updates at most once a day) and queried lazily, so creating a class is instant and filters only read what they need. show_options went from about 8 seconds to 0.1 seconds, and select is faster too. Results are still pandas DataFrames with to_toolkit(); pass as_pandas=False to get a Polars DataFrame instead.
  • Typed Parquet files. The published data now also comes as Parquet, with delisted stored as a real boolean, so nothing has to be converted after loading. The bz2 CSV files are still published unchanged, so older versions of the package keep working.
  • The ticker NA (Nano Labs) is no longer read as a missing value.
  • Restructured internally into helpers, models and controllers, the same layout as the Finance Toolkit. Public classes and methods are unchanged.
  • Requirements: Python 3.11 or newer (3.11 to 3.14 are supported), financetoolkit>=2.2.1, polars>=2.0, pandas>=3.0, plus numpy and requests, which were already used but are now declared. The PyPI page now links to the homepage and repository.

Database

Comparing the published data of 2.4.0 with 2.5.0 (live listings, so delisted ones excluded):

2.4.0 2.5.0
Equities with an ISIN 26% 78%
Equities with a FIGI 43% 80%
Equities with a sector / industry 62% / 41% 95% / 88%
Equities with a website / headquarters city 39% / 41% 86% / 86%
Equities with a market cap tier 44% 88%
Equities with a description 60% 95%
ETFs 36,483 44,429
ETFs with an ISIN 22% 37%
ETFs / funds with a fund family 75% / 64% 84% / 72%

Added. Close to 15,000 equity listings that were missing, taken from official exchange symbol directories and confirmed on OpenFIGI: among others 1,135 Shanghai and Shenzhen listings, 935 on the Bombay Stock Exchange, 748 in Taiwan (including TSMC), 578 in London, 468 in Korea, 362 in Warsaw, about 500 each from the Middle East, Europe and Asia-Pacific, Nasdaq First North, new NSE and ASX listings and US OTC lines. About 8,000 ETFs were added (US and international, including UCITS listings), plus open-ended funds and Bitcoin pairs for the cryptocurrencies. New listings come in with their company description, address, website, market cap tier and a sector, industry group and industry classification, and the weekly update now also reads the official exchange directories.

Corrected.

  • Every equity and ETF ISIN was verified on OpenFIGI. ISINs, CUSIPs and FIGIs that belonged to another company, share class or exchange were cleared or replaced, for example local listings that carried their foreign parent's or ADR's identity, such as Infosys, Siemens India and Oracle Japan.
  • Hundreds of renamed companies now carry their current name and description on all their listings, for example Avolta (formerly Dufry), Clariane (Korian), CMB.Tech (Euronav) and PDD Holdings (Pinduoduo).
  • Tickers that were replaced by a new ticker, or that no longer trade anywhere, are flagged as delisted. That's about 17,000 equities, kept for reference; exclude_delisted hides them.
  • Market cap tiers were refreshed with current market caps, and secondary listings use the tier of the company's home listing.
  • Websites, descriptions and classifications that belonged to a different company were fixed.
  • All-caps and truncated exchange names such as "SIEMENS AG NA O.N." are written as proper company names.
  • ETFs are categorised with one documented system based on their holdings (see CONTRIBUTING.md). 168 airport, port and toll-road operators are classified as Transportation Infrastructure.
  • Postcodes follow each country's format, damaged characters are repaired, and every classification is checked against the classification tree (scripts/categories.json) in the test suite.

Moved. Listings are in the asset class the rest of the database uses for them: exchange-traded products and funds filed as equities moved to the ETF and fund files (Leverage Shares ETCs, Gold Bullion Securities, Danish investment funds), and REITs and other companies filed as ETFs moved to equities.

Removed.

  • About 35,500 empty equity records without a name or any other information, most of them on Euronext.
  • About 15,500 instruments that are not stocks: certificates, turbos, covered warrants, structured notes and dated bonds, for example Vienna and German bank certificates and Korean warrants.
  • About 10,900 empty index records and 158 empty money market records.
  • Duplicate listings written in two notations (for example BRK/A next to BRK-A).

Maintenance

  • The weekly update adds new tickers from official exchange directories and stops re-adding share classes written with a slash.
  • Pull requests now run the classification check and an identifier validation, and the tests compare the package against the data in the pull request itself.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.4.0
html:
Even though not much in the package itself changed there are major new additions to the database itself, these are the main topics:

EXPANDED METADATA
Added hundreds of thousands of new entries across Equities, ETFs, Funds, Indices, Currencies, and Cryptocurrencies. These are fields such as business summaries, sectors, industry groups, and categories for precise filtering and screening.This goes alongside new company IPOs. There now also exists a delisted flag that indicates whether the company is delisted or not.

DATA QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS
Resolved conflicting company names, refined existing categorizations, and completely re-evaluated existing mappings. This includes adding over 15,000 new ISIN and CUSIP codes to significantly improve database precision. Furthermore, the equities, funds and etfs datasets now have been split up in exchanges (before compression) so PRs are easily reviewable.

IMPROVED ROBUSTNESS
Upgraded the core Python package to handle edge cases and invalid inputs gracefully, ensuring a seamless integration with tools like the Finance Toolkit. Furthermore, there exists now a delisted filter that automatically filters out companies that have the delisted flag set to True.

What's Changed

  • Bump fonttools from 4.58.5 to 4.61.0 by @dependabot[bot] in #117
  • fix: correct and enrich 229 ISIN codes in equities database by @AlfaStake in #126
  • Add ISIN codes for ETFs by @AlfaStake in #124
  • Bump pillow from 11.3.0 to 12.1.1 by @dependabot[bot] in #123
  • Bump protobuf from 6.31.1 to 6.33.5 by @dependabot[bot] in #121
  • Added SCMB by @pettijohn in #135
  • Added some missing currencies and names from SEC Data by @pettijohn in #136
  • Backfill ~4.5k CUSIP values in equities.csv from SEC 13F filings by @dokson in #138
  • Backfill ISIN/CUSIP + fix placeholder names from yfinance by @dokson in #139
  • Fix 1,084 placeholder names + 614 country + 35 exchange from yfinance by @dokson in #141
  • Replace 725 boilerplate summaries with yfinance longBusinessSummary by @dokson in #142
  • ASE exchange fix + ISIN/FIGI backfill from public data by @dokson in #143
  • Fill 17,252 empty exchange + market cells in equities.csv by @dokson in #145
  • Baseline test improvements: snapshots, local data, docstrings, infra cleanup by @dokson in #140
  • Test infra follow-ups #2: library invariants, helpers.py coverage 45→86%, cov in CI by @dokson in #146
  • ETFs/Funds data quality + cross-asset invariants + equities country/ISIN backfill + SPAC cleanup + README stats by @dokson in #147
  • Add mic_code (ISO 10383 MIC) column by @dokson in #149
  • Enrich composite_figi and fill mic on new tickers by @dokson in #150
  • Enrich FIGI via OpenFIGI, add 709 tickers (#119), fix README stats workflow by @dokson in #151
  • Added delisted column into the database and split up the equities, funds and etfs files by @JerBouma

New Contributors

  • @AlfaStake made their first contribution in #126
  • @pettijohn made their first contribution in #135
  • @dokson made their first contribution in #138

Full Changelog: 2.3.1...2.4.0

name: FinanceDatabase 2.3.1
html: This is a minor release that fixes the issue as reported in #108. I've also updated the database with the suggestion from #107.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.3.0
html:
The latest release of FinanceDatabase (v2.3.0) significantly expands the quality of the database and the ability to better parse through the 300.000+ entries as found in the database with the related financedatabase package.

I've added hundreds of thousands of new metadata entries across Equities, ETFs, Funds, Indices, Moneymarkets, Currencies, and Cryptocurrencies. These are fields such as summaries, sectors, industry groups, industries, category groups, categories, and currency and more. This allows for more precise and granular classification for better filtering, grouping, and analysis.

I've also updated the associated Python package by adding more robustness, handling edge cases and invalid inputs more gracefully. Upgrade now to v2.3.0 with pip install financedatabase -U.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.2.0
html:
This release features the introduction of the FinanceFrame. This is a DataFrame with extras, namely the function to_toolkit. As also visible in this example, the Finance Database can now directly convert the symbols to the Finance Toolkit 🛠️ making it possible to do combine the exploration of tickers from the Finance Database with the in-depth financial analysis from the Finance Toolkit.

As an example, it is possible to use both .select() and .search() and combine this with .to_toolkit().

For fundamental data, you need to obtain an API Key from FinancialModelingPrep. This is used to gain access to 30+ years of financial statement both annually and quarterly. Note that the Free plan is limited to 250 requests each day, 5 years of data and only features companies listed on US exchanges.

Obtain an API Key from FinancialModelingPrep here.

Through the link you are able to subscribe for the free plan and also premium plans at a 15% discount. This is an affiliate link and thus supports the project at the same time. I have chosen FinancialModelingPrep as a source as I find it to be the most transparent, reliable and at an affordable price. I have yet to find a platform offering such low prices for the amount of data offered.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.1.1
html: This release makes it possible to filter by multiple criteria for the same columns. Next to that, many company names are adjusted in the database that contained accented characters.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.1.0
html:
This release includes over 9.000 ISIN codes, more than 25.000 FIGI codes and more than 2.000 CUSIP codes. This is a start to not only allowing you to work with tickers (like MSFT which is Microsoft Corporation) but also with ISIN (US5949181045), FIGIs (BBG000BPHFS9) and CUSIP (594918104) codes.

Furthermore, I have also updated the exchange names being much more clear now. Lastly, made a small bug fix when you wish to work with the database locally.

name: FinanceDatabase 2.0.0
html:
I've improved this database not only by increasing the amount of symbols (from 180k to 300k) but also:

  • Introduced the database's own classification of equities into sectors, industry groups and industries.
  • Updated and removed tickers that either no longer exist or had outdated information.
  • Made the package itself object orientated making data collecting and searching much more efficient and logical. (shoutout to Colin Delahunty for the help here too)
  • The database initially featured thousands of JSON files. At the time it made sense also given my rather novice background in programming. However, a much more efficient (and manageable way) is to work with CSV files. So instead, one CSV file per asset class
  • Due to using CSV files, it becomes really easy to update accordingly.
  • To make loading data itself still quick, it automatically compresses the data so that loading in data is not slowed down by using a format that is more easy to update.
  • Updated the README, Contributing Guidelines and overal documentation.

name: FinanceDatabase 1.0.0
html: Added market cap to Equities and total assets to ETFs and Funds. Furthermore, renamed the package to financedatabase (from FinanceDatabase) to be more in line with PEP8.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.11
html: In this release I have included a parameter called exclude_exchanges. By default this paramater is set to True which means all exchanges are excluded from the selection (via for example select_equities). This is done to prevent the user from receiving several times the same ticker (but in different exchanges). Setting this parameter to False returns the amount of tickers as listed in the Key Statistics in README.md

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.10
html: Added the possibility to point to a different URL as well as the option to select a local location. Furthermore, fixed a small bug in the select_etfs function and added test cases to ensure for a more robust package.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.9
html: A significant update has occurred to the Database. This required some changes to the package attached to it. Primarily splitting up the large Equities JSON file as it exceeded the 100MB limit of GitHub as well as removing the Options and Futures categories. These were time dependent and thus serve no value in a week or two.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.7
html: Improved the search function to allow more flexibility. You are now able to search in any key of the dictionary by changing the parameter 'search'. Also, by default the query is not case sensitive. Thus both STOXX and stoxx would yield the same result. The variable 'case_sensitive' can be set to True to change this.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.6
html: Fixed an issue where if you only add 'equities' to show_options, it wouldn't work. Now it gives you countries, industries and sectors in separate dictionaries.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.5
html: Make equities_selection an optional parameter in show_options.

name: FinanceDatabase 0.1.4
html: First release of the package, prior versions had some minor bugs in them.
